articles.description: Every NFL team's win total, as well as odds to win the division, the conference and Super Bowl LXI.
articles.headlineJa: 第61回スーパーボウル優勝オッズ：全32チームの優勝確率
articles.descriptionJa: 全NFLチームの予想勝利数、およびディビジョン、コンファレンス、第61回スーパーボウルでの優勝オッズ。
articles.body:
For the first time this season, the Los Angeles Rams are not the favorites to win Super Bowl LXI, as they have fallen to +700 after beginning the campaign at +500. The division-rival San Francisco 49ers are the new favorites at +620, having shortened after coming out of Week 5 tied with the Rams.

L.A.'s latest loss came via an overtime thriller Monday night to the Buffalo Bills, who are tied for the third-best odds on the board with the Baltimore Ravens at +800.

The next tier includes the Kansas City Chiefs, who lengthened slightly from +900 to +950 during their bye week, and the Seattle Seahawks, who fell from +950 to 11-1 week-over-week after their close loss to San Francisco and are now 12-1 following Thursday's loss to the Denver Broncos (20-1).

The Jacksonville Jaguars continue to gain ground after beginning the season at 30-1, making it all the way to 12-1. The undefeated Minnesota Vikings have also been a notable improver, tied with three other teams at 20-1 after coming into the campaign at 50-1.

The season's biggest disappointment is undoubtedly the Los Angeles Chargers, who began the season with sixth-best 17-1 odds and have fallen virtually out of contention to 200-1 after an 0-5 start.

Note: Odds by DraftKings  and subject to change.

Each week during the 2026 NFL season, these fantasy football IDP rankings will be updated by fantasy analysts Mike Clay, Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Moody.

articles.headline: Arsenal's Mikel Arteta defends Viktor Gyökeres after goalless start to season
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has defended Viktor Gyökeres amid criticism of the Arsenal striker's start to the season.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has defended Viktor Gyökeres amid criticism of the Arsenal striker's start to the season.

Gyökeres arrived last summer in a €73 million (£61.5m) deal from Sporting CP and scored 14 Premier League goals as the Gunners won the title for the first time in 22 years.

However, Arsenal spent the summer scouring the market for another attacking option with Atletico Madrid's Julián Álvarez among their leading targets with reports in Spain suggesting Gyokeres could have been used as a makeweight in a potential deal.

Arsenal were unable to prise Alvarez away from Madrid and opted not to sign a forward with Arteta preferring Kai Havertz to Gyökeres in the club's biggest games so far this season.

Gyökeres is yet to score in seven appearances this term but Arteta believes that was close to changing in his 65-minute display against Lille on Tuesday night.

Speaking on Friday ahead of the weekend trip to Nottingham Forest, Arteta said: "These are moments in a player's career, or in a season I would say. We are trying to help him as much as possible.

"The other day, he had some very good moments. He was three or four times in front of goal with no keeper, the ball should arrive to him and it doesn't and maybe you are talking about something else.

"But these are the strikers. It is very small margins. Scoring or not scoring changes the narrative, for sure not the perception how much he can help the team."

Gyökeres had just 12 touches and failed to register a shot against Lille.

- Arsenal's Mikel Merino: I am 'fortunate to be alive' after Dortmund bus attack

- Arsenal's Eberechi Eze to perform Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired celebration after loss to IShowSpeed

Havertz is expected to return to the starting line-up at the City Ground and when asked whether Gyökeres is suffering from a lack of confidence, Arteta said: "That's a very person question. What he transmits is an incredible will and determination and work rate to improve and help the team.

"That's Viktor every single day regardless of his position, whether he scored a goal or not. And that's why he's always an option to play."

Arteta confirmed Piero Hincapié is still "a week or two" away from returning to action following an ankle injury while Martín Zubimendi [also ankle] is progressing well and could be available within the next week.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick denies divisions within Man United squad after Lisandro Martínez outburst
articles.description: Michael Carrick has insisted there are no divisions within the Manchester United dressing room after Lisandro Martínez criticised the strength of the squad.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick has insisted there are no divisions within the Manchester United dressing room after Lisandro Martínez criticised the strength of the squad.

Martínez has apologised after his barbed comments aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox following the 2-0 defeat to Atlético Madrid on Tuesday.

The Argentina defender also suggested the squad was not good enough to compete in the Champions League.

It prompted Wayne Rooney to say the post-match interview could "rip the dressing room apart." But Carrick said he had no concerns about a rift among the players.

"It's done really," Carrick told a news conference on Friday.

"We've moved on from that. It's really not a drama for us as a group. I have to say, they were in really good spirits and trained really well, so we've moved on pretty quickly.

"There's a lot of people that say a lot of things, and ex-pros or not ex-pros, it doesn't necessarily mean you understand what's going on here.

"Just because people talk from the outside, that doesn't mean that's the truth. I'm telling you the truth. The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I've seen it for a while, actually."

United head to Leeds United on Sunday on a run of five games without a win.

The poor form has put pressure on Carrick, but the 45-year-old said the eventful week could end up bringing the players closer together.

- Man United's Martínez issues apology for post-match outburst after meeting

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

- UCL Matchday 2: Viking FK and PSG impress; Man United a mess

"Certain situations, it can galvanise the group, and it's certainly galvanised the group as this week's progressed," he said.

"The boys are, I have to say, in a really good place right now.

"I don't need results. I don't need results, we all need results. It's not about me, you know? It's not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player, anyone else who works at this football club.

"Whatever's best for the football club and for the team on Sunday is the most important thing, it really is not about me."

articles.headline: Florian Wirtz form can improve if Liverpool drop him - Steven Gerrard
articles.description: Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has said that Florian Wirtz "coming out of the team" could be the solution to his confidence and form improving after a disappointing start to the season.
articles.body:
Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard has said that Florian Wirtz "coming out of the team" could be the solution to his confidence and form improving after a disappointing start to the season.

Wirtz -- who was one of Liverpool's marquee signings last summer -- completed a move worth £116 million ($156.27m) from Bayer Leverkusen but supporters are still waiting for the highly-anticipated arrival to live up to his price tag at Anfield as patience wears thin.

The 23-year-old is yet to score a goal for Andoni Iraola's side this season despite featuring in every game, managing only his second assist on Thursday, when he set up Bradley Barcola's second goal in the Reds' 6-3 win over LASK in the Champions League.

"His confidence is short at Liverpool at the moment and you can see it when you watch him live," former Liverpool midfielder Gerrard said on The Overlap. "He's giving the ball away, simple balls that he wouldn't give away.

"I have had dips in form and lack of confidence and the best thing for me was to come out of the team for periods of time.

"And when someone is playing in your position you start going 'oh he might take my place' and you get that little bit of fear and then you have to build your consistency in training and then it starts coming out in games."

Wirtz started in the No. 10 role in Liverpool's 3-0 defeat to Manchester City in the Premier League on Sunday but failed to impress and was the first player to be withdrawn following Ryan Gravenberch's red card despite the home side desperately needing a goal.

Asked whether pulling Wirtz out of the team is the solution to the player's improvement in form, Gerrard said: "That might be the thing that makes him go 's--- my place is gone' and that's what you fear. It's happened to me.

"The problem Liverpool have is [Hugo] Ekitike is missing, [Alexander] Isak's been a bit flakey as of late, [Cody] Gakpo's injured so at the moment you probably can't do that. But when you start getting a few bodies back, I don't think it will do him any harm to come out.

- Why do Liverpool's big-money transfers keep failing to deliver?

- Trey Nyoni backed by Liverpool's Andoni Iraola amid midfield injury issues

- Premier League Top 50: Ranking the best players so far this season

"He needs to be looking at his clips in training and in games, the balls he's giving away and needs his staff and manager to grab him, he's a talent, he's young, you can't give up on these people. He needs help and he needs support."

Gerrard was asked how much more time the German international should be given to succeed at Anfield.

"I'd say at the end of the season if the form is still the same and he is still underperforming and he's not delivering after he's had two seasons, I think it's a bit different then," Gerrard said.

Wirtz scored seven goals in 49 appearances for Liverpool last season.

articles.headline: Shakhtar's Champions League win vs. AEK was more than just a game
articles.description: Shakhtar Donetsk haven't played at home since 2014 due to the war, and this season, their Champions League home games are at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Wednesday's win was a reminder of how absurd their situation is.
articles.body:
LONDON -- Take a step back and revel in the absurdity for a minute. Shakhtar Donetsk, a Ukrainian team from the Russian-speaking part of the country, are playing a Greek team, AEK Athens, in London, at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Technically, it's a "home game," but that concept has become rather meaningless.

Shakhtar haven't played at their home, the Donbas Arena, since May 2014, some 650 weeks ago. They turn up wherever someone will host them: Odessa, Kyiv, Kharkiv and Lviv for Ukrainian league games; Warsaw, Hamburg, Gelsenkirchen, Krakow, Ljubljana and now London for matches in European competition. Why? Because their opponents can't (or won't) travel to Ukraine, where none of the civilian airports are open, air raid sirens go off a dozen times a day, and where drones and bombs can't be trusted to distinguish between a military captain and the captain of a soccer team.

It's pretty obvious that in those circumstances, you're more than a club -- you're a symbol of defiance, an attempt to maintain some sort of normality in the face of a war that has taken more than half a million lives and displaced tens of millions more.

"We are playing for people from Ukraine all over the world," sporting director Dario Srna said. "Everywhere we've gone, they've come [to see us]. We represent Ukraine in the center of the world: we're not just playing for us. [We are] a Ukrainian team, we are not just Shakhtar."

But, of course, nothing is normal. Everything is messed up, and their mere presence in the Champions League constitutes a political dimension.

Wednesday night, Shakhtar were at Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea. Resourceful as ever, street vendors outside the ground hawked their off-brand scarves, except rather than "Cole Palmer," "João Pedro" and "John Terry," the names read "Pedrinho," "[Mykola] Matviyenko" and "[Valeriy] Bondar." Watching over them was a life-size cardboard cutout of Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, only his face was replaced by that of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy.

Inside, visiting AEK fans -- who turned the Shed End into a two-tier wall of tifo, flags and noise -- outsing, if not outnumber, the "home" support.

Because yes, this is Shakhtar's home for the Champions League this season, a move made possible by the London club's failure to qualify for European competitions (and, probably, a need to rake in some extra rent on those empty weeknights). Ironically, Chelsea's previous owner, Roman Abramovich, was forced by the U.K. government to sell the club after the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, because of his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Abramovich holds passports from Portugal, Israel and Russia. His yachts are moored in Turkey.

Abramovich, whose mother is Ukrainian, is a complicated figure. So is Shakhtar's version of Abramovich, Rinat Akhmetov.

Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae is on the radar of Arsenal, while Liverpool are in pole position to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Arsenal are interested in signing Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae during the January transfer window, reports Bild's Christian Falk. The Gunners are seeking defensive cover following an injury to Piero Hincapié, though the 29-year-old South Korea international could also be offered a contract extension to remain in Bavaria.

- Liverpool are in pole position to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, according to the Daily Mail. The 23-year-old, whose transfer is valued at £100 million, has drawn widespread interest from major clubs including Chelsea, though he is currently sidelined after sustaining an injury on his full England debut.

- Should a January deal for Scott fall through, Liverpool have compiled scouting dossiers on Monaco's Lamine Camara and Roma's Manu Koné, TEAMtalk reports. However, the Reds face competition for €55 million-rated Camara -- with Chelsea maintaining interest alongside Aston Villa, Newcastle United, Crystal Palace and Brighton & Hove Albion -- while Koné has been linked with Real Madrid, Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United.

- USMNT prospect Mathis Albert is considering leaving Borussia Dortmund to secure regular first-team minutes, according to Sky Sports Deutschland. The 17-year-old winger has only made one appearance in the German Cup this season. He previously attracted interest from Paris Saint-Germain in 2025, while Manchester City and Chelsea were also looking at signing him for around €20 million.

- Tottenham Hotspur will demand a £75 million fee to consider letting right back Pedro Porro move to Barcelona or Real Madrid, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old signed a five-year contract extension in the summer, significantly strengthening Spurs' position as they aim to retain him past 2027.

articles.headline: Premier League Top 50: Ranking the best players so far this season
articles.description: The Premier League Top 50 returns for the 2026-27 season to rank the best players across the league so far.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグ・トップ50：今シーズンこれまでのベストプレーヤーをランキング
articles.descriptionJa: 「プレミアリーグ・トップ50」が2026-27シーズンに復活。リーグ全体でこれまでに活躍した最高の選手たちをランキング化します。
articles.body:
Let's dig into the big question that's on everybody's mind: Who, uh, is the best player in the Premier League?

While we wait for the league to issue its punishment to Manchester City for breaking 114 rules and cheating their way to a spend of $1 billion more than regulations allowed, the games still go on.

Did you know Jordan Henderson scored twice last week? For Chelsea? Also: None of the promoted teams are in the relegation zone! Hull City are tied for seventh! Everton ... are tied for fourth?

To take stock of what has suddenly become -- and will continue to be -- the weirdest Premier League season of all time, we've decided to roll out the second edition of ESPN's Premier League Top 50, with our first coming before the season began.

We'll ask it again: Who is the best player in the Premier League? And now we'll answer it.

How we rank the players and who missed out

As we've done for the past two years, the rankings are meant to be a combination of true talent, how much value a player has actually provided and how much better that player is than the average players at his position.

The list is still tilted toward goal-producing-and-creating players on the best teams in England, but it opens up space for defenders and midfielders and goalkeepers from a bunch of different places up and down the table.

Injured players are ineligible, so you won't see the likes of Arsenal's William Saliba, Liverpool's Hugo Ekitike or Bournemouth's Alex Scott on the list.

You also won't see Liverpool's Bradley Barcola, who I'd expect to be on the list by the end of the season, but who has had almost no impact on any of the Premier League matches he has played thus far. A couple of other new signings -- Barcola's club and country teammate Jérémy Jacquet and Aston Villa's record signing Johan Manzambi -- have already broken into the top 50 with impressive starts to their Premier League careers.

Unless otherwise noted, most of the data you'll see throughout the piece comes from the stats app Futi. OK, let's get to the top 50...

50. Thierno Barry, striker, Everton

There's a great new book by David Epstein called "Inside the Box." It's, essentially, about how we tend to be at our best -- whether on our own or as groups -- where we're forced into constraints.

There are infinitely more options at our disposal today compared with 30 years ago; constraints help with that problem. But they also seem to make us more creative, more productive and happier.

See: Everton Football Club. Last summer they signed a promising young striker from Villarreal with a nice track record of getting lots of high-quality shots. But he was mostly a backup behind the veteran Beto, who left this offseason.

Everton tried to sign U.S. men's national team standout Folarin Balogun on the final day of the transfer window -- only for it to fall apart because of issues Everton had with Balogun's medical clearance exam.

articles.headline: Maxey: Healthy Embiid 'changes everything' for Sixers
articles.description: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.
articles.headlineJa: マクシー：「健康なエムビードがいれば、シックスターズのすべてが変わる」
articles.descriptionJa: 76ersのガード、タイリース・マクシーは木曜日、ジョエル・エムビードが健康であることがシックスターズにとって「すべてを変える」と語った。
articles.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey said Thursday that having a healthy Joel Embiid "changes everything" for the Sixers.

Embiid's 10-year career has been marred by injury. He has never played a full 82 games and has played more than 60 games just four times in his career. Over his 10 seasons, he has averaged just 49 games per season, which doesn't include him missing his first two seasons with injury.​

Embiid played just 38 games last season, double his number from 2024, as he navigated right hip complications, left knee management and appendicitis. The injuries have often kept Embiid out of training camp and the preseason -- crucial time for a team to get comfortable playing with a player like Embiid, the 2023 NBA MVP.

"You can put in more packages," Maxey said. "There's been times where he hasn't been healthy and we get into the game and now we're trying to learn on the flow."

Maxey said his experience gives him the advantage. He knows where Embiid likes to catch the ball, where he wants guards to cut and other tendencies that he has learned over six years of playing together. But many of the Sixers' new additions, most notably among them LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, don't have that luxury.

The difference this year is that they had a healthy Embiid in training camp and the preseason to make that transition easier.

​"If you haven't been playing with a big like Joel, there's not many. It's very hard, very difficult to learn certain things," he said. "...So, with him being here, we can drill those things over and over. It's been what, like two, three weeks that we've had just drilling and drilling. That's a good thing."

At the end of last season, Embiid said he was "as confident as I've ever been" about his health moving forward.

"I think, obviously, [my knee] was the biggest concern, and I'm not thinking about it," he said. "And as long as we keep doing what we've been doing, I won't have to think about it anymore.
